parole.significato: a small to medium-sized bag, usually of fabric
parole.testo: From Middle High German biutel, from Old High German būtil, from Proto-West Germanic *būdil (“bag, purse”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰew- (“to blow, swell”). Cognate with Dutch buidel, Yiddish בײַטלען (baytlen).

From Middle High German hecke, from Old High German hegga, from Proto-West Germanic *haggju, from Proto-Indo-European *kagʰyo-. Cognate with Dutch heg, English hedge.

From Middle High German kiver m or n, from Old High German kifer, from Proto-West Germanic *kebr, from the perhaps onomatopoeic Proto-Indo-European root *ǵep- (“to chew, eat”), also the root of Käfer (“beetle”). Compare the Proto-Indo-European roots *ǵyewh₁- (“to chew”) and *gʰabʰ- (“to seize”).

From Middle High German stuol, from Old High German stuol, from Proto-West Germanic *stōl. Cognate with Dutch stoel, English stool, Swedish stol; ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂- and thus related to stehen.
From Middle High German trūre (“mourning”), from Old High German trūrēn (“to mourn”), from Proto-West Germanic *drūrēn (“to fall”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dʰrews- (“to break apart”).
Attested since the 12th century, from Middle High German treppe, trappe, from Old High German trappa, from Proto-West Germanic *trappā.

parole.significato: angle, nook; corner (seen from the inside)
parole.testo: From Middle High German winkel, from Old High German winkil, from Proto-West Germanic *winkil (“angle, corner”), from Proto-Indo-European *weng- (“to bend, bow, arch, curve”). Cognate with Dutch winkel, Old English wincel.
